Mail.app compatibility and acceptance

SpamWise targets macOS 27 and Apple Mail. The package and app require Swift 6.4 / Xcode 27 for development. Builds and runtime checks in this repository used an Apple-silicon Mac. Intel execution and older macOS versions are unverified; do not lower the deployment target as a compatibility claim. Apple's on-device classifier also requires Apple Intelligence availability and downloaded model assets. Provider availability is checked at runtime and never causes a silent model substitution.

Observed account behavior

The evidence below is from signed-app probes recorded in CLAUDE.md and the live Mail follow-up on October 16, 2026. It describes those probes, not blanket provider certification or acceptance of all parity features.

Mail.app account Apple Events connection Inbox/Junk round trip Orange flag Offline/reconnect New parity workflows
iCloud Passed Passed at 08:42 PDT, with 30-second settling per move Passed Pending Confirmed Junk/read, historical preview, renamed-folder fail-open, closed-window/relaunch scanning observed
Google Passed Passed at 08:45 PDT, with 30-second settling per move Passed Pending Pending
Exchange / Microsoft 365 in Mail Not tested Not tested Not tested Not tested Not tested
Other accounts in Mail Not tested Not tested Not tested Not tested Not tested

The cross-account probes avoided duplicate Message-IDs in the receiving account's Sent mailbox. Same-account duplicates remain ambiguous and untouched. An earlier immediate self-mail move was unstable and appeared in Recovered Messages; subsequent settled cross-account probes passed. Thirty seconds is an observation interval, not an independent server acknowledgement.

Mail's account-specific special Inbox/Junk roles are used for moves; SpamWise does not guess a destination by name. Accounts → Mailbox destinations reads those roles without reading message bodies or enabling actions. Names alone do not prove Gmail system labels. During authorized probe cleanup, Mail's Google Trash role mapped to a custom Deleted Messages folder; operator cleanup required exact-message Gmail system TRASH verification. The product exposes no Trash/delete action. A Junk role must be validated on its own, not inferred from the behavior of another role.

Incoming routes

The signed Apple Events route polls Mail.app and supports bounded account/folder sweeps. It needs SpamWise and Mail running on an awake Mac, Automation permission, and available message sources. Keep dry run enabled for comparisons with SpamSieve and server rules. Their classifications and folder membership are not human labels.

A signed incoming delivery updated both MailKit heartbeat and body timestamps at 23:21:45 PDT, approximately two seconds after receipt. An earlier delivery encountered stale extension generations (PlugInKit “other version in use”); a graceful Mail restart and re-registration of the installed extension preceded the successful observation. Stable account identity and timing under server-routed Junk, delays and cancellation are still unvalidated. MailKit remains dry-run only; one successful callback does not establish delivery coverage.

Repeatable acceptance matrix

For each configured account, use uniquely identified, disposable cross-account mail and retain its exact identities. Record initial role mapping, delivery time, first scan time, decision path, source mailbox, intended action and settled outcome. Exercise Inbox delivery, server-routed folders, no MailKit callback, repeated sweeps, restart, wake, reconnect and a changing multi-page mailbox. Compare two filters with SpamWise in dry run first. Never send ordinary Junk through training automatically.

New workflows also need explicit selected corrections, Junk restore, mark-as-read, dedicated training-folder placement from a second device, and renamed/missing-folder checks. Only generated messages may be used for action probes. Clean up their exact received/Sent/draft copies when finished, without emptying Trash or touching ordinary Junk. Preserve unexplained gaps and uncertain actions as failures, not successes.
